benchmark_version: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v3.0.0 (control numbers change between versions)

5.1.title: Ensure That Cloud Storage Bucket Is Not Anonymously or Publicly Accessible
5.1.why_it_matters: Granting allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers on a bucket lets anyone on the internet read its contents.
5.1.how_this_project_addresses_it: The scanner flags public IAM bindings and buckets without public access prevention. The remediator enforces public access prevention, which blocks public access even if an allUsers binding remains. Removing bucket-level bindings is not automated; the allowlist skips them and a human reviews the drafted fix.

5.2.title: Ensure That Cloud Storage Buckets Have Uniform Bucket-Level Access Enabled
5.2.why_it_matters: Uniform bucket-level access removes per-object ACLs, so a bucket that is not public cannot have public objects.
5.2.how_this_project_addresses_it: The reports bucket and the Terraform state bucket are created with uniform bucket-level access, and the demo bucket uses it too.

1.5.title: Ensure That Service Account Has No Admin Privileges
1.5.why_it_matters: A service account with Admin, Editor or Owner roles can do far more than its job needs, so a leak or bug has a large blast radius.
1.5.how_this_project_addresses_it: cspm-scanner uses a custom role with only the permissions it needs. cspm-agent has only table-level BigQuery roles, jobUser, and access to a single secret.

1.6.title: Ensure That IAM Users Are Not Assigned the Service Account User or Service Account Token Creator Roles at Project Level
1.6.why_it_matters: At project level these roles reach every service account in the project, including future ones, which allows privilege escalation.
1.6.how_this_project_addresses_it: Token Creator is granted to the operator on each specific service account, never at project level.
